Important buying advice

Choose true D-size cells. Some inexpensive rechargeable D batteries contain smaller AA cells inside, greatly reducing capacity.

Check voltage. Most NiMH rechargeable D batteries are 1.2V, compared with 1.5V for alkaline batteries. Most devices tolerate this, but not all.

Get a compatible charger. Make sure it explicitly supports D-size NiMH cells.

For emergency storage, prioritize low self-discharge rather than maximum advertised capacity.

My pick: Tenergy Centura for emergency use, or Tenergy Premium 10,000mAh for devices used regularly.

What are you using the D batteries for—flashlights, camping lanterns, automatic trash cans, baby swings, or something else? That could change which one I'd recommend.
